title: Signed 64-bit arithmetic right shift
summary: Recovered the 33-byte compiler helper at VA 0x8fc260 from accepted assembly and direct Game.exe disassembly. Input/output uses EDX:EAX and count uses CL. Caller evidence at 0x59b22d and 0x5cbf01 confirms the ABI. Portable unsigned arithmetic preserves sign extension without undefined full-width shifts. Only the low count byte is used; values 64 through 255 saturate to the sign. No fields, memory accesses, imports, FS use, or external dependencies occur.
test_description: Direct original reference calls through GCC i386 regparm(3), returning EDX:EAX. Compares 12 boundary/pattern inputs across counts 0..1023 and high ECX bits, all 64 one-bit and complemented one-bit inputs across all 256 CL values, and 10000 deterministic pseudorandom values/counts. No object fields or memory side effects exist to preserve, as verified by instruction inspection.
known_limits: Portable C++ API replaces the compiler-private register ABI; original scratch ECX and condition flags are not exposed.
Behavioral recovery only; no matching-byte claim.
